YouTube Data API v3: API key, quota and pricing

📅 Nov 26, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Posted on Nov 26 • Originally published at handlesapi.com

You get a YouTube API key by creating a Google Cloud project, enabling YouTube Data API v3 in it and generating a key on the Credentials page. The steps below follow Google's getting started guide as of November 2026.

Treat the key as a server-side secret. Anyone who holds it spends your project's quota. This is Google's own request for a channel's statistics by handle:

Every Google Cloud project starts with a YouTube Data API quota of 10,000 units a day, and the counter resets at midnight Pacific time (quota cost table). Each method spends a fixed number of units per call.

Source: Google, determine quota cost and the search.list reference, as of November 2026.

Many guides still say a search costs 100 units. That changed. Since 1 June 2026, search.list costs 1 unit but lives in a separate bucket limited to 100 calls a day, according to the method's revision history. For creator discovery or any search-driven tool, that cap binds first.

A worked budget, as an illustration. Refreshing 5,000 channels once a day with channels.list uses 5,000 units, half the default quota, and leaves 5,000 for video reads. A discovery job that runs 150 searches a day is over the search cap by itself, whatever is left of the 10,000 units.

To raise the limit you apply for it. Google starts with a compliance review through the Audit and Quota Extension Form, so plan for a review step before launch if you expect volume.

Google does not list a per-call price for the YouTube Data API; the cost is the quota. There is no meter to pay down, but once the daily units are spent, further calls are refused until the counter resets.

That makes the real price a mix of engineering time and review time: a Cloud project to maintain, keys to rotate, quota to budget across jobs, and an audit if you outgrow the default. For one app reading a few thousand channels a day that is usually fine. For a pipeline that sweeps tens of thousands of channels, the unit budget and the search cap shape the architecture.

Handles API meters in credits instead of quota units. A catalog read costs 1 credit and a live read costs 2 credits, and a failed call is not charged. The Free trial is 100 credits once, with no card. Details are in credits and limits and on the pricing page.

One more date to note: since 16 November 2026, co-views count toward public view counts, per the YouTube Data API revision history. If you store a view series yourself, mark that date so a step in the data is not read as organic growth.

Handles API reads public YouTube channel data from its own catalog of about 97K channels, over one REST key. The table compares it with the official API on what matters when you are choosing between them. It is an independent service, not affiliated with Google or YouTube.

Official column from Google's YouTube Data API documentation, as of November 2026. Credit and plan figures from Handles API plans.

This is a real catalog response for the same channel as the official request above, captured from the live API. Note the fields: counts, hidden_subs, language, country and category.

Real response from the live API, captured Nov 26, 2026. 10 more record fields trimmed for space. Long strings and arrays are shortened.

For a first batch of 1,000 catalog reads, plan costs work out like this.

Plan price divided by included credits. A catalog read costs 1 credit, a live read 2 credits. The Free trial is 100 credits once, no card.

Rate limits work per minute rather than per day. The Free plan allows 10 requests a minute, and paid plans run from 120 to 1,200 a minute. Pagination on list endpoints uses a cursor you follow until it is null, described in pagination.

Use the official YouTube Data API whenever you need more than public channel numbers. It is the right tool for:

Know the limits of a catalog before you rely on it. Records are as fresh as the last crawl, and each carries a last_seen timestamp so you can check. Private data, writes and channels that are not in the catalog are out of reach, and the Free trial of 100 credits is a good way to test coverage on your own list of channels first.

Use a data API when the job is reading public stats for many channels, ranking them or tracking them over time, and you would rather budget credits than quota units. Nothing stops you from using both: the official API for writes and owner data, Handles API for read-heavy stats.

The same question comes up on other platforms. See the Instagram Graph API comparison and the TikTok Research API comparison. For the wider picture of collecting public social data, including the rules, read social media scraping: methods and limits.

Create a project in the Google Cloud console, enable YouTube Data API v3 from the API Library, then open the Credentials page and choose Create credentials and API key. Send the key as the key parameter on requests for public data. Methods that act for a signed-in user need OAuth 2.0 instead.

The default quota is 10,000 units per day for each project, reset at midnight Pacific time. Reading a channel with channels.list costs 1 unit and so does videos.list. Since June 2026, search.list has its own bucket: 1 unit per call, capped at 100 calls a day.

Google does not list a per-call price for the YouTube Data API. The cost is the quota: once the daily units are used, further calls are refused until the reset. A higher limit is not bought, it is requested through a compliance audit using the Audit and Quota Extension Form.

As of November 2026, one search.list call costs 1 unit, not the 100 units older guides quote. The catch is that searches count against a separate Search Queries bucket that allows 100 calls per day, so search-heavy tools hit that cap long before the 10,000 unit quota.

Yes, with a data API that serves public channel records from its own catalog. Handles API needs only its own key and a credit balance, with no quota units to manage. It is read-only and covers about 97K channels, so uploads, comments and OAuth data still need the official API.

Sandscale has two MCP servers, and the docs describe both: a remote server at https://mcp.sandscale.dev/mcp, and sandscale mcp, a local server that comes with the CLI. They talk to the same sandboxes and the same audit log, but they are different programs with different tool lists. This post lays them side by side so you can pick one, or decide to run both.

Sources: the Connect Claude or ChatGPT guide, which carries the remote server's tool table, and the MCP tools reference and sandscale mcp CLI page for the local one. Both tool lists are generated from the servers themselves, so they are the place to check if this post goes out of date.

Sandboxes. Both servers can list, start, run commands in, and stop sandboxes.

So only the remote server can pause, resume and snapshot over MCP. If your agent's workflow is "install dependencies once, snapshot, start each task from the snapshot", the remote server is the one with the tools for it. The snapshots guide covers what a snapshot keeps.

The local sandbox_start takes template, ttl and network inputs, and its description says the network is none unless asked. sandbox_exec takes the command as an array of strings, plus optional workdir and timeout_seconds. The remote server's sandbox_run returns the exit code, standard output and standard error.

Files. Remote only: sandbox_upload_file (text in content, bytes in content_base64) and sandbox_download_file (text back as text, other bytes as base64). With the local server, an agent moves data with commands, or you move files with the CLI yourself.

Workspaces. Both. Remote: workspace_list, workspace_start, workspace_stop. Local: workspaces_list, workspace_show, workspace_start, workspace_stop. A workspace is a persistent cloud computer; stopping it keeps its disk.

Storage and Vault. Remote only: storage_list_buckets and storage_describe_bucket for your S3-compatible buckets, and vault_list_secrets, which lists secret names in a Vault KV mount. Values are never returned by any Sandscale MCP tool.

Build hosts and lab hosts. Local only, and read-only: build_pools_list, build_leases_list, build_lease_show, build_lab_hosts_list. If an agent needs to see which build machines or lab devices you have leased, this is the server.

Both servers keep secrets away from the model. The remote server lists Vault names but never values. The local server's reference is broader: signing in, the vault and deleting anything are not offered as tools at all.

The remote server's docs also spell out what it cannot do: act as anyone else, go unrecorded, or run without limits. Each app can make up to 120 calls a minute and each person up to 60. Every remote call is in the organization's audit log with the tool, region, outcome and app, and never the arguments.

A coding agent on your laptop (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, Windsurf). Either works. Choose the remote server if you want file upload and download, pause, resume and snapshots as tools, or if you do not want to install anything. Choose the local server if you already use the CLI, want build host and lab host visibility, or prefer the server whose reference says it offers no tools for signing in, the vault or deleting anything.

A hosted assistant (Claude or ChatGPT on the web). Only the remote server, added as a custom connector. There is no local process for a hosted assistant to start.

Shared setups. The remote entry contains no secret, so a project config file that points at it (.mcp.json for Claude Code, .cursor/mcp.json for Cursor, .codex/config.toml for Codex) can be committed. Each person still signs in as themselves. The local entry is just sandscale with the argument mcp, and depends on each person's CLI sign-in.

Both at once. Nothing stops you adding both under different names, for example sandscale and sandscale-local. The cost is a longer tool list for the model to choose from, and two tools with similar names (sandbox_run and sandbox_exec) that do roughly the same thing. If you do it, use your client's allow and deny settings to keep only the tools you want from each.

Whichever you pick, the calls end up in the same place. The remote guide says every tool call goes through the same API, permissions, plan limits and audit log as everything else, and refusals come back with the API's own error code. The local reference says each tool runs the matching sandscale command with your own sign-in, so every check and refusal is the command's. In both cases your role, your plan and your organization's policy decide what happens, not the server you came through.

Atalanta, Sarri: "Tante palle gol ma fragili dietro. Scamacca-Krstovic? Nessun dualismo"

📅 Nov 26, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Al termine della folle rimonta dell'Atalanta sul campo del Borac Banja Luka, vinta per 3-2 negli ultimi sette minuti grazie alle reti di Krstovic all'86', Kolasinac al 90' e Zappacosta al 93' in una sfida valevole per la quarta giornata della fase a campionato di Conference League, il tecnico nerazzurro Maurizio Sarri è intervenuto ai microfoni di Sky Sport per analizzare la partita.

Una serata che siete riusciti a raddrizzare soltanto nel finale, probabilmente i sette minuti più pazzi da quando allena l'Atalanta. Le chiedo una lettura di una partita per certi versi senza senso, perché dopo un buon inizio siete andati sotto di due gol e poi nel secondo tempo siete riusciti a risalire.

"La verità è che abbiamo fatto una buona partita e abbiamo creato tantissime palle gol. Purtroppo in questo momento non abbiamo solidità difensiva e questa fragilità ci fa diventare tutte le partite più complicate. Però, se guardi i numeri della gara, le occasioni nostre ci sono: negli ultimi sette minuti abbiamo fatto tre gol su quattro palle abbastanza facili, mentre nei dieci minuti precedenti avevamo sbagliato tre reti da un metro. Oggi abbiamo combinato errori in fase risolutiva e continuiamo ad avere qualche problema difensivo. Detto questo, è chiaro che la partita diventa complicata, ma la squadra ha dimostrato grande carattere come negli ultimi tempi. Bisogna lavorare per risolvere il problema che ci rende le sfide così difficili. Voglio dire un grazie anche ai nostri tifosi che hanno fatto tanti chilometri per essere qui e che per novantasette minuti ci hanno dato veramente una mano: per fortuna stasera li abbiamo ripagati."

Come si trova la solidità difensiva oltre che con il recupero di Kossounou e Hien, che di fatto non ha mai avuto?

"Bisogna lavorare, ricercare e ricavarsi dei tempi di lavoro che, fra gli infortuni e il calendario, per noi sono difficilissimi da trovare. Però bisogna riuscire a farlo sia a livello di reparto difensivo, sia a livello di squadra."

Soprattutto nel primo tempo mi sono sembrate esserci un po' di ripartenze legate a letture preventive non eccezionali non soltanto dei difensori, ma anche dei centrocampisti, mentre nel secondo tempo sono stati un pochino più attenti.

"Sì, io ho parlato di linea difensiva ma anche di fase difensiva. Le distribuzioni sotto la linea della palla e qualche lettura della linea non sono state sicuramente di buon livello. Questo si sta ripetendo da diverse partite e ci crea delle difficoltà: poi le gare per noi si complicano e non possiamo sperare di risolverle sempre così."

Mi sposto sull'attacco, perché è inevitabile ragionare su un eventuale dualismo tra Scamacca e Krstovic, visto che il tabellino racconta l'importanza dell'ingresso di quest'ultimo. Le chiedo se Krstovic, al di là delle qualità dei singoli, sia forse più adatto in questo momento per il tipo di squadra che sta costruendo a Bergamo.

"Non so, io prima dell'inizio della stagione avrei risposto che Scamacca è un giocatore adattissimo a me. È un centravanti fisico ma allo stesso tempo molto bravo tecnicamente e abile a venire a giocare con la squadra. La differenza in questo momento è che uno è in pieno ottimismo e in piena condizione psicofisica, mentre l'altro viene da un momento molto difficile e piano piano sta cercando di ricostruirsi. L'ho sempre detto: secondo me il dualismo non esiste, con me partono alla pari e poi è il campo a decidere chi gioca di più. In questo momento sta facendo meglio Krstovic e gioca di più Krstovic, però potrebbe essere anche solo un momento stagionale."

Dawn of War 4 writer John French lays out how it works.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The original Dawn of War's Winter Assault expansion added campaigns that let you play two factions at once, with different final missions based on which one you triumphed with. Dawn of War 2's campaign was even more player-led, with distress calls that had different outcomes based on what you prioritized and, in the Chaos Rising expansion, a morality mechanic with Corruption and Redemption points. It even chose a different character to be a traitor based on who gained the most Corruption by the story's end.

I asked John French, Dawn of War 4's writer and a Warhammer novelist, whether Dawn of War 4 would follow this noble tradition by having player decisions alter the plot. "The player's decisions very much change the perspectives that they'll experience the game from," he replied. "So, depending on which heroes from each faction they choose, they'll have a very different experience of the game, in that they'll see different parts of the story and sometimes different views on the same events."

Based on what we've seen of the Ork and Adeptus Mechanicus campaigns, that means partway through you'll be presented with a choice between two Commanders who have opposed goals and the one you pick will lead to missions with different objectives. Ork Beastboss Guzcutta is trying to unite his clan, the Snakebites, while his rival warboss, Gorgutz, is an off-world interloper trying to rebuild his damaged invasion force.

"With characters like Gorgutz and Guzcutta," French explained, "it can be as simple as one of them wants to do it the traditional, brutal ork way, and one of them wants to do it in a brutal but cunning way, so you have missions that focus on getting lots of shiny kit in one, while the other tries to get as many orks to follow them as possible.

"In a more complex narrative, like the Adeptus Mechanicus campaign, Potentia-Delta-9's main drive is the quest for knowledge, and she is on a very different path from Skitarii Marshal Sek-Ix-23, who is very much about enforcing the orthodoxy. The story for both overlaps, but which character you choose and what decisions you make with them lead down different experiences of an overlapping story."

Writing an RTS isn't all about plotting out the campaign missions. The Dawn of War games are legendary for their unit barks, like the saber-rattling Lord Commissar who shouts, from the top of an armored Chimera transport, "Drive me closer, I want to hit them with my sword!" Getting across so much personality in a short space is a real skill.

"You can do an awful lot with just a couple of words like 'More dakka!'," French said, "that tells you a huge amount about the orks on its own. Even with factions like the necrons, the way that the lower ranks respond to the higher ones with just 'Obedience,' one word, tells how their faction works."

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Part of the appeal of Warhammer is the berserk variety of its armies, each with its own highly thematic identity. You walk into a shop and see the stoic space marines alongside spiky Chaos daemons and units of Astra Militarum who look like they stepped out of a trench in World War I before being given laser rifles.

"Dawn of War 4 is deeply Warhammer in that way because it's got all of these different textures of factions and characters next to each other," French said. "You have orks, and they are absolutely fixated on smashing everything they can in the pursuit of trying to have an even bigger fight. Then you've got the Adeptus Mechanicus, who revere machines as holy and worship the machine as god with complete sincerity and total conviction. Those two things literally exist side by side, along with alien races who have made themselves immortal by creating metal bodies with hyper advanced technology. And all of these different types of character come into conflict on one planet cut off in a sea of night—that's very Warhammer."

Dawn of War 4 is due out on December 3 and will be available on Steam. Owners of the Commander Edition will get advance access and can play from November 30.

Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames, Zed Games. He's written for Rock Paper Shotgun, The Big Issue, GamesRadar, Zam, Glixel, Five Out of Ten Magazine, and Playboy.com, whose cheques with the bunny logo made for fun conversations at the bank. Jody's first article for PC Gamer was about the audio of Alien Isolation, published in 2015. Jody edited PC Gamer Indie from 2017 to 2018, and he eventually lived up to his promise to play every Warhammer videogame.

Nvidia Is the Worst-Performing "Magnificent Seven" Stock This Year. Is It a Buy Before 2027?

📅 Nov 26, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Even with Jensen Huang back as CEO, Nvidia is drastically underperforming the S&P 500 and Nasdaq this year.

By Daniel Foelber – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:30PM EST

Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) investors have been on a rather unenjoyable roller coaster in recent weeks. And every time the ride looks like it's nearing an end, there's another unexpected turn that unearths more questions than answers.

Founder and CEO for over 33 years, Jensen Huang, admitted on Nov. 8 to being unfaithful to his wife, then resigned on Nov. 12, only to be brought back as CEO less than two weeks later on Nov. 23.

That same day, President Trump was on a phone interview with CNBC and took credit for speaking with Nvidia's board and helping convince them to bring Huang back. Trump said, "I spoke to them. Let me just put it that way. And I convinced them. And I will tell you, it was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week and a half ago." Trump was referring to Nvidia's stock price and how it was easier to convince Nvidia to bring Huang back when the stock was cratering.

Nvidia has rallied substantially since Huang came back as CEO, but Huang and Nvidia still face an uphill climb of federal, state, and internal investigations linked to Nvidia misleading investors and potential national security violations regarding advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence (AI) chips leaking into China through backdoor channels.

The stock is still under $100 per share at the time of this writing and down 20% year to date -- making it the worst-performing "Magnificent Seven" stock in 2026. The Magnificent Seven consists of seven mega-cap tech-focused companies that include Nvidia, Apple (AAPL +0.43%), Microsoft (MSFT -1.25%), Alphabet (GOOG -2.02%) (GOOGL -2.13%), Amazon (AMZN -3.12%), Meta Platforms (META +3.40%), and Tesla (TSLA -1.18%).

Here's the simplest reason to buy Nvidia, and an argument for why it's best to keep the semiconductor stock on a watch list for now.

Heading into this year, some investors were concerned that Nvidia would be unable to maintain its breakneck revenue growth rate and high gross margins. But hyperscalers continued to ramp up AI capital expenditures. And Nvidia has broadened its customer base to other enterprises, AI start-ups, AI labs, and neoclouds.

As a result, Nvidia's earnings growth began outpacing its stock price growth, compressing its valuation. But then the unthinkable happened.

Nvidia's stock price has plummeted despite exceptional results and guidance for 75% revenue growth in fiscal 2028. Nvidia reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 17, with revenue more than doubling from the third quarter of fiscal 2026. In the nine months ended Oct. 25, 2026, Nvidia generated $183.3 billion in net income compared to $77.11 billion for the nine months ended Oct. 26, 2025.

Nvidia is on track to surpass Alphabet as the world's most profitable company. It now trades at just 15.4 times forward earnings -- making it the cheapest Magnificent Seven stock despite having the highest gross margins and the fastest revenue growth rate.

For context, the forward P/E of the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.25%) is 17.3 -- meaning Nvidia is now priced like a value stock.

Buying high-quality companies on sale is an excellent way to compound wealth over time. Nvidia doesn't have to deliver blowout results to impress investors. In fact, its growth rate could fall substantially, and it would still be a steal at current levels.

The issue isn't Nvidia's valuation -- it's investors' concerns about where the company could be headed over the next three to five years.

Jensen Huang's sudden resignation exposed Nvidia's extreme vulnerability to key-person risk, governance failures, and an incapable board of directors. Going forward, Nvidia will need to change its structure to be less dependent on Huang, which could make it more rigid and less innovative but also protect long-term investors.

In addition to Nvidia-specific issues, there's also the risk that AI spending could decline considerably due to higher interest rates, which have made borrowing more expensive. With democrats taking control of the Senate and the House, there may be higher regulatory hurdles to accelerating data center construction. And there's the ongoing risk that compute demand will taper off as AI models become more efficient.

Granted, Nvidia is incredibly well positioned to endure a slowdown because of its industry-leading position and rock solid balance sheet. But it could also lead to stagnating or declining earnings in the medium term, which would challenge Nvidia's valuation.

All told, Nvidia simply has too many unknowns right now. Until investors get more clarity on the findings of the investigations, the company's succession plan for Huang, and the extent of its governance overhaul, Nvidia remains a hold.

Heading into the new year, I'd rather buy high-quality Magnificent Seven stocks with a clear runway for future earnings growth like Alphabet, even if its valuation is more expensive than Nvidia's.

Each of these mattress toppers softened up our hard beds, but there's a clear winner for the ultimate in cooling side sleeper comfort (and it has a big Black Friday price cut too)

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

While Saatva, Tempur-Pedic, and DreamCloud are offering the best Black Friday mattress deals we've seen this year, all three brands are also behind some of 2026's best mattress toppers. But which premium mattress topper should side sleepers buy in the Black Friday sales?

We've tested the Saatva Graphite, Tempur-Adapt + Cooling and the DreamCloud mattress toppers and they each deliver the signature luxury of their respective brands' mattresses. This comparison guide will help you choose which topper is right for you if you're a side sleeper in need of extra comfort.

For the latest price cuts, also see our guide to the best Black Friday mattress deals live.

A comfy topper from a leading sleep brand, but its retention of excess heat lets it down. Though if feel cold in bed, this could be ideal.

The 3"-thick Graphite Memory Foam Mattress Topper is the most popular entry in Saatva's bed topper collection. Its body-cradling foam supports all sleep positions, including side sleeping, while its anchor straps keep the topper in place. However, despite the infusion of graphite, this memory foam topper can trap body heat.

Sink-in softness, contouring that hugs your curves to relieve pressure, and all-night cooling to keep you at the right temperature for sleep.

The Tempur-Adapt + Cooling is the most top-rated mattress topper we've ever tested, as it uses Tempur-Pedic's propriety Tempur-Material to provide softening comfort for side sleepers and hard beds. The addition of a cooling cover prevents heat build-up, but be aware that there's no official sleep trial.

A good cooling memory foam topper to soften the area under your shoulders, hips and knees, but the lack of anchor straps is frustrating.

The DreamCloud Softer Mattress Topper is made from a 2" slab of gel memory foam that our testers found to be cushioning along the shoulders and hips, making it ideal for side sleepers. Its breathable cover complete with "cooling yarns" means the DreamCloud Topper doesn't overheat. However, there's no anchor straps to prevent shifting.

All three mattress toppers are 3" thick and use memory foam to cushion firm beds. While each works well for side sleepers, their distinct features make them better suited for different types of side sleepers.

For instance, the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Mattress Topper caters to all sleep styles, making it ideal for side sleepers who sometimes switch to back or front sleeping — or side sleepers who share a bed with someone who sleeps in a different position. In contrast, the DreamCloud and Tempur-Adapt have a plush feel best suited to side sleepers only.

The Tempur-Adapt + Cooling Mattress Topper has a cooling cover to prevent side sleepers from overheating (the Saatva Graphite, on the other hand, is prone to heat build-up). The DreamCloud Softer Mattress Topper also sleeps cooler than the Saatva Graphite, but doesn't have the washable cover with anchor straps. Still, it's the cheapest of the three, starting at $179 (the Saatva starts at $225; the Tempur-Adapt at $259).

We test mattress toppers in key areas, particularly in temperature regulation and comfort and support. We then give each area a score out of 5.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

When testing comfort and support, our testers sleep on each topper in the three main sleep styles (back, side, and stomach) to see how comfortable and supportive it is in each position. The Saatva Graphite performed the best in this area, scoring a near-perfect 4.5/5, because its medium-firm feel supports all sleep styles.

In comparison, the Tempur-Adapt's 3.5/5 score may seem low, but that's because it's too soft to support back and front sleepers. For side sleepers only, the Tempur-Adapt + Cooling provides incredible pressure relief. The DreamCloud also lost a point for its softness, but it's still a great topper for side sleepers.

As for temperature regulation (how well a topper maintains a comfortable temperature), the Tempur-Adapt's cooling cover upgrade scored the highest points. Meanwhile, the DreamCloud's breathable cover, while not cool-to-the-touch, prevented overheating. The Saatva Graphite scored the lowest, as our lead tester found it was prone to trapping heat.

Here's a close-up look at each mattress topper, exploring their respective designs and prices, plus who we do and don't recommend them to...

The Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Mattress Topper is a 3" slab of graphite-infused memory foam that's enveloped in a breathable, antimicrobial organic cotton cover (the same material used for the covers of the best Saatva mattresses).

Despite a naturally cool cover and a graphite-infusion, our testers found the Saatva Graphite's memory foam to trap heat. However, both Saatva customers and our testers agree that the memory foam's medium-firm feel adds plenty of comfort and support to mattresses.

The Saatva Graphite (or any other Saatva toppers, for that matter) are pretty much never included in the Saatva Black Friday sales, let alone the monthly Saatva sales. That means you'll always pick up a Saatva Graphite from $225 in a twin. Extras include a generous 180-night sleep trial and a so-so one-year warranty.

The 3" Temur-Adapt + Cooling Mattress Topper is actually an upgrade of the original Tempur-Adapt Mattress Topper. We found the original's use of pressure-relieving Tempur-Material was great for side sleeping, but was also prone to heat build-up.

That's why were so pleased when the + Cooling upgrade added a cooling cover, with out lead tester impressed with the difference it made. While not a great mattress topper for those who sleep on their back or front, it's a top pick for side sleepers who need to soften hard beds.

The Tempur-Adapt + Cooling Topper is the only one out of the three toppers to be included in the Black Friday mattress topper sales. This means you'll save up to 30% on all sizes in this month's Tempur-Pedic sales, with a twin now down to $259 (was $339). Disappointingly, there's no sleep trial, but you will get a generous 10-year warranty.

DreamCloud is known for its flagship DreamCloud Classic Hybrid, a luxury hybrid mattress at a medium-range price, so it's only fitting that it would offer a bed topper at a fraction of the cost of its mattresses, too.

The DreamCloud Softer Topper is one of two DreamCloud toppers; the other is called the DreamCloud Firmer Topper, which is designed to give a (you guessed it) a firmer feel. The DreamCloud Softer Topper is made from 2" of gel-infused memory foam, which our testers say provides a contouring feel for side sleepers.

The DreamCloud Softer Topper may not be on sale for Black Friday (no surprises there, it's never in the DreamCloud sales) but that doesn't stop it from being the cheapest option. A twin is priced at $179, and comes with a 100-night sleep trial, a one-year warranty, and free shipping and returns.

For side sleepers who are looking to soften a hard bed, we'd reccomend looking at the Temour-Adapt + Cooling or the DreamCloud Softer Topper. Both have a plusher feel than the Graphite and are great at regulating temperature, though those who need a bigger comfort boost should go for the thicker Tempur-Adapt.

Those looking for the most cost-effective, on the other hand, should pick the under-$200-for-a-queen DreamCloud. Meanwhile, the Saatva Graphite is best for side sleepers who prefer a firmer feel, combination sleepers, and couples with different sleep styles.

Microsoft-owned developer platform Github stepped in it earlier today when it posted a message on X celebrating the success of AnyPS5, an open source project that aims to let users port PS5 executables to PC, and then linked that success directly to efforts to port Grand Theft Auto 6 to PC. The message was deleted shortly after it was posted, but not before it was widely noticed and called out for being a very bad idea.

"GTA 6 is finally here, sparking one of the biggest weeks in gaming and open source on Github," the message stated (via Kotaku).

"The repo AnyPS5 has passed 58K stars since its August launch, rewriting PS5 executables to run on Windows and Linux. Does changing where games run cross a legal line? Share your take. Happy GTA VImas!"

Lest there be any misunderstanding, a video that accompanied the post made the GTA 6 connection explicit: "The project rewrites a game's executable so Windows and Linux can run it directly. Performance seems to be the main issue for users wanting to run GTA 6, with one contributor telling the project's community to 'lock in and get your agents to help' if they need to."

And here's the accompanying video from @github's GTA6 tweet https://t.co/crU9cpOWcsNovember 26, 2026

The question of whether or not this sort of thing crosses a legal line has, predictably, sparked debate among those who think they have a clear understanding of the answer. What caught most by surprise, though, is that Github—which is owned by Microsoft—would put forth the question in the first place, implicitly suggesting that it might not. GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive has been pretty aggressive with its efforts to keep recompiled versions of GTA 6 from landing on PC, and I can't imagine it would too thrilled with Github—which, I must emphasize, is owned by Microsoft—telling the world that it might actually be okay to go ahead and vibe-code it up.

That point wasn't missed by redditors, one of whom described it as Github "openly taunting Sony and Rockstar." Even the AnyPS5 subreddit seemed baffled: Redditor superkickstart asked, "Do they have AI running their socials? Lol"

There's also a little bit of irony in the fact that, until earlier this week, the leading effort to get GTA 6 running on PC was based on an Xbox build of the game posted by GTA 6 leaker Cyberleeks. Beyond that, there are also some very obvious questions about how Github (owned by Microsoft) would react to AI-powered ports of, say, other software:

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The whole thing is weird, really, because it seems like such an obviously bad idea. The only explanation I can come up with is that a social media manager either didn't think about it, didn't understand it (which would be weird in itself for someone doing social media posts for Github), or just had a big ol' brain fart. Whatever the reason, I imagine someone got a good old-fashioned talking-to about it.

I've reached out to Github and Take-Two for comment and will update if I receive a reply.

'The Walking Dead' Meets 'War of the Worlds' in Noah Wyle's Gritty 5-Season Sci-Fi Thriller

📅 Nov 26, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

If aliens took over our world tomorrow, what would America look like months down the line? That's the exact question that the Steven Spielberg-produced TNT drama Falling Skies aimed to answer, and it did just that over five stellar seasons. Something of a cross between the sci-fi aesthetics of War of the Worlds and the apocalyptic character drama of The Walking Dead, this underrated cult classic deserves a rewatch — and now that it's on Netflix, there's no better time than the present.

Part of what set Falling Skies apart from the get-go was that it didn't begin with the invasion. We don't see the military's first attempt at defending our world as the major cities across the globe, Boston in this case, are descended on by alien overlords with less than admirable intentions. In step with The Walking Dead, although the world before is referenced at first, the show doesn't take long to throw you into the "new normal" that these horrid circumstances have created. When we first meet Tom Mason (played by Noah Wyle, who did double duty on this show and The Librarians during the latter's first season), for instance, he has already lost one son to these invaders on top of his wife. Although he was a history professor, he's now been conscripted as the second-in-command of the 2nd Massachusetts militia led by Col. Dan Weaver (Will Patton). We're not privy to how all that played out, but it doesn't matter. This is where the story begins.

While the show is unashamedly science fiction in the same vein as War of the Worlds, it's structured much like The Walking Dead in practice. Each episode follows this unlikely band of militia warriors on weekly quests to find new supplies, uncover more intel, or save a captive they've recently seen enslaved by the invaders. Of course, the show becomes a bit more serialized as time goes on, but many of those early episodes are spent establishing the characters so that when tragedy does strike, it means something. As the widowed father of three boys — Hal (Drew Roy), Ben (Connor Jessup), and Matt (Maxim Knight) — Tom has more to lose than just about anyone, and yet continues to help lead the fight against the Espheni in the same ground-up style as the American Revolution.

The cast is further rounded out by pediatrician-turned-jack-of-all-trades doctor Anne Glass (Moon Bloodgood), who herself has suffered serious loss at the hands of the invaders. As Tom and Weaver take the fight to the aliens on the literal battlefield, Anne works to uncover the secrets of their biology. Her part in the war is pivotal, as learning all they can about their new enemy gives the 2nd Mass the power to work against them. And, how could we forget about Colin Cunningham's John Pope? The motorbike-style outlaw became a vital part of the show throughout the entirety of its run, often standing in stark contrast to Tom and his morally conscious methods of warfare. Often butting heads, the pair each found ways to contribute to the 2nd Mass — and thus the war — that led to some impressive developments.

Falling Skies always thrived in the visual department. While some of the CGI may look a bit hokey now, back in 2011 when the show first premiered, the alien mechs and the Espheni were crafted quite well and blended effortlessly into the torn-down world around them. The alien creatures, such as the Skitters and the Volm, the alien race led primarily by Tom's friend and ally Cochise (Doug Jones) beginning in the third season, were likewise constructed with feature-level quality, using a blend of practical effects with digital enhancements. As much as we watched Falling Skies (which was already underrated in its day) for its characters and to see how the battle against Earth's first extraterrestrial invaders would play out, there was always something magnetic about the aliens and the battle sequences that ensued.

Although one might argue that Falling Skies was a stronger show early on (and there may be some truth to that), the TNT drama ultimately concludes on its own terms. Across five seasons and 52 episodes, the post-apocalyptic sci-fi series builds toward an inevitable conclusion that pits Tom and the 2nd Mass against the overlords trying to wipe out and enslave the human race. It's a powerful (and profound) climax that feels earned, and proves to be worth the journey. Falling Skies was a summer show, airing in the three-month break between traditional television seasons, which meant that it was always welcomed back by fans with open arms. All these years later, it still packs a serious punch for folks looking for something as patriotic as it is sci-fi-flavored.

Falling Skies is available for streaming on Netflix.

Celtic player ratings: Camilo Durán rescues team of low marks as one starter stands out

📅 Nov 26, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Colombian’s late header ends Celtic’s 23-year Portuguese hoodoo in gritty Torreense triumph

Celtic clinched a vital 2-1 Europa League victory over second-tier outfit Torreense, thanks to an 84th-minute header from substitute Camilo Duran that ended the Scottish champions' 23-and-a-half-year wait for an away win on Portuguese soil.

Played nearly 50 miles away from Torreense’s 2,431-capacity home at Estadio Manuel Marques, which fails to meet UEFA stadium criteria, the 24,000-seater Municipal Stadium in Leiria was dominated by roughly 4,000 travelling Celtic supporters, making up two-thirds of the crowd. Despite the partisan backing, Martin O’Neill’s men made remarkably hard work of overcoming a side sitting 13th in Portugal’s second division with just two league wins from their opening ten matches.

There is an old adage in European football that fortunes earned by accident are rarely retained by design. For 45 disjointed minutes, Celtic offered a textbook demonstration of the principle. Handed an early advantage through the sort of comical defending usually reserved for Scottish clubs on their continental travels, Martin O’Neill’s side promptly retreated into their shell, allowing Portuguese second-tier minnows Torreense to restore parity and seize the initiative before the interval.

Celtic’s precarious Europa League campaign was balanced on a knife-edge. Having opened their league-phase campaign with three consecutive defeats before salvaging a breathless 3-2 victory over Beşiktaş in Glasgow earlier this month, O’Neill’s men arrived in central Portugal languishing in 32nd place.

Anything less than maximum points against a Torreense side operating in the lower reaches of Liga Portugal 2, yet remarkably seated 19th in this competition with six points following last season’s improbable Taça de Portugal triumph, threatened to render Celtic’s remaining fixtures against Omonia, Marseille, and Union Saint-Gilloise an exercise in mathematical futility.

O’Neill had cautioned on the eve of the tie that his squad lacked the pedigree to indulge in complacency. Initially, however, the evening appeared set to unfold with uncharacteristic smoothness for the Scottish champions.

Restored to the European squad as an injury replacement for Mika Baur, Jota marked his return to his homeland with immediate industry down the left flank. Inside nine minutes, the winger collected possession near the by-line and whipped a low, enticing delivery into the six-yard box. With Yang Hyun-jun hovering intently at the back post, Torreense full-back Javi Vázquez panicked under pressure, slicing his attempted clearance past his own goalkeeper and into the net.

It was a moment of extreme generosity, yet Celtic proved remarkably ungrateful recipients. Rather than using their early cushion to assert authority, the visitors lapsed into a passive, defensive shell. Though Celtic commanded the majority of possession, they managed to invite pressure rather than alleviate it.

Torreense, a club steeped in modest provincial history rather than continental glamour, sensed the vulnerability. Vázquez nearly atoned for his earlier mistake in the 17th minute with a venomous, low free-kick from a narrow angle that required hasty defensive intervention. Two minutes later, the equaliser duly arrived, born of Celtic’s chronic inability to clear their lines.

Given acres of space 20 yards from goal, midfielder Álex Alfaro unleashed a fierce drive that crashed against the underside of Sam Johnstone’s crossbar. As the ball dropped invitingly inside the penalty area, Celtic’s backline froze. Kieran Tierney’s tentative, lofted clearance succeeded only in teeing up Dany Jean, and the forward exhibited admirable composure to dart past Colby Donovan and drill a low finish beyond Johnstone’s reach.

Jota remained Celtic’s sole reliable source of invention. Celtic’s solitary threat to reclaim the lead prior to the break arrived on the stroke of half-time, when the Portuguese star's deep cross was hooked back across the face of goal by Luke McCowan, only for Kasper Høgh to arrive a fraction too late to apply the finishing touch.

Jota nearly restored the lead within seconds of the restart, only for his attempted dink to be gathered by a scrambling Adriel. But as the hour mark approached, Celtic’s frustration grew.

Former Hearts striker Musa Drammeh nearly dealt a massive blow to their hopes of progressing to the knockout stages by shrugging off a feeble challenge before dragging a golden chance narrowly wide of the far post.

James Forrest took over from the impressive Jota in the closing stages and the substitution proved to be a masterstroke. With Celtic seemingly sleepwalking toward a damaging result, Forrest swung a pinpoint cross in from the right, and Duran peeled away at the back post to power a downward header past Adriel. It was the Colombian’s 15th goal of a remarkable campaign, once again rescuing his side.

McCowan missed a late one-on-one opportunity to add a touch of gloss to the scoreline in the 89th minute, seeing his tame finish saved by Adriel’s boot. However, it did not matter. For the first time since O’Neill’s side triumphed at Boavista in April 2003, Celtic left Iberian soil victorious.

The Odyssey's New Release Shuts Down The Last Remaining Concern About Nolan's Masterpiece

📅 Nov 26, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

The last rumbling concerns surrounding Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey have been put to rest with its latest release. Christopher Nolan has spent much of his career making films that demand to be experienced on the big screen. From the rotating corridors of Inception to the spectacular aerial sequences of Dunkirk and the enormous practical effects of Oppenheimer, his film-making style has always benefited enormously from theatrical presentation.

The Odyssey is perhaps his most ambitious attempt yet to make audiences appreciate the possibilities of large-format cinema. Based on Homer's ancient Greek epic, the 2026 blockbuster follows Matt Damon's Odysseus as he attempts to return home to Ithaca following the Trojan War, confronting mythical creatures, dangerous gods, and extraordinary obstacles along the way.

Its enormous scale and extensive use of IMAX photography made seeing it in a premium theatrical format particularly rewarding, while its spectacular imagery helped distinguish it from other recent blockbusters. Naturally, bringing such an ambitious production into the home presents some challenges. Fortunately, the new 4K release addresses the biggest remaining concern about experiencing Nolan's latest masterpiece outside the cinema.

Universal released The Odyssey on 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray and digital platforms on November 17 with a 1.78:1 aspect ratio, filling a conventional widescreen television. The theatrical IMAX presentation used the taller 1.43:1 ratio, meaning the home version loses a small amount of image at the top and bottom.

Despite what some purists might assert, this makes virtually no difference to the viewing experience, with no noticeable loss of important visual information. Furthermore, the 4K transfer brings out the textures of the enormous practical sets, the detail in the costumes, and the natural beauty of the locations. The sequences involving Odysseus' ships, the vast battlefields of Troy, and the dangerous open sea still look spectacular, even without the enormous IMAX screen surrounding the audience.

Obviously, watching The Odyssey at home cannot replicate the sheer scale of a 70mm IMAX screening, particularly when Ludwig Göransson's score and the film's enormous sound effects are filling a cinema auditorium. Indeed, IMAX is designed to be as immersive as possible with sound and vision. While no home viewing experience can replicate this, The Odyssey’s sharp 4K imagery is a pretty close domestic alternative.

One of the most rewarding things about revisiting The Odyssey is having the opportunity to appreciate Christopher Nolan's storytelling without being quite so overwhelmed by the spectacle. The theatrical experience is deliberately enveloping, with enormous set pieces, elaborate action sequences, and Göransson's thunderous score commanding attention. It's part of the appeal, but it can also make it difficult to appreciate some of the smaller details on a first viewing.

At home, there's more opportunity to concentrate on the performances and the relationships driving the story. Matt Damon's Odysseus is a particularly interesting protagonist because his journey is about far more than surviving dangerous encounters. It explores loyalty, identity, and the consequences of war – which all become easier to appreciate when the immediate visual spectacle isn't quite so overwhelming.

Robert Pattinson's performance also benefits from another viewing, as does the film's elaborate treatment of Homer's mythology. The supporting characters and the various encounters along Odysseus' journey contribute to a larger story about the difficulty of returning home after becoming somebody fundamentally different.

Universal's physical release also includes 12 behind-the-scenes featurettes, covering everything from the construction of the Trojan Horse and the enormous Moroccan battlefield sets to the film's practical effects, stunts, and Göransson's score. These extras offer another reason to revisit the production, particularly for anyone interested in Nolan's commitment to large-format film-making. No matter the aspect ratio, The Odyssey is a truly extraordinary cinematic achievement.

Apple’s best wireless earbuds have dropped to their cheapest price yet, taking a full $100 off the standard price tag. Alongside improved audio quality, stronger active noise cancellation, and extra battery life, you’re getting a redesigned, more comfortable build engineered for a secure fit.

In our Bose QuietComfort Headphones review, we said these are "excellent always-on noise-cancelers with enhanced sound and battery life." Featuring over-ear active noise cancellation, switchable Quiet and Aware modes, and long-lasting battery life, they’re built for uninterrupted listening wherever your day takes you.

With AirPlay, DTS Virtual:X, Dolby Vision, and an AI 4K upscaler, the Hisense QLED E6 is a great budget choice. And at $172 off (55-inch version), this TV is a stellar option for upgrading your living room for much, much less.

If you've been intrigued by lifestyle TVs but hesitant about their relatively high price tags, the discounted Hisense S7 Canvas TV might be the set you've been waiting for. It's adorned with an elegant, replaceable, teak-style frame, its screen features a matte finish, and it offers an entire Art Gallery for displaying works of art when not in use.

In our Hisense U6SF Pro review, we called the U6 Pro one of the best budget Mini-LED TVs out there. All models are on sale, but the 75-inch model is such an epic bargain at this price point. Two of its four HDMI inputs feature 2.1 functionality (like support for 4K games up to 144Hz), and the screen is outfitted with a glare-free finish that actually works. If you're on a budget, enjoy mostly daytime viewing, and are an avid gamer, this TV is for you.

The Sony Bravia 6 OLED is up to $1,600 off for the 83-inch panel. This premium TV has Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, 4 HDMI 2.1 ports, is capable of displaying over a billion colors, and has bass reflex speakers.

Keep track of all your stuff with Apple's own Bluetooth tracker, whether it's a bag, wallet or your keys. The new generation AirTag features instant pairing, a speaker that's 50% louder, and improved Precision Finding to help you hunt down your missing items with more accuracy.

The iPad (11th Gen) is a great option for kids or anyone who just wants a simple tablet for surfing the web, playing videos and playing less demanding games. It's the best Apple tablet for most people to own and Black Friday is unquestionably the time to pick one up. In our iPad 11 review, we said it has significantly improved performance thanks to its A16 chip, longer battery life, and a larger 128GB starting storage option; Apple's entry-level tablet is among its best.

Like with the Nintendo Switch 2 above, the MacBook Neo received a price hike this year. Apple upped the price by $100, but this Amazon deal slices half that right back off again. It's still Apple's most affordable Mac and, for students or anyone wanting a reliable macOS machine, it's one of the strongest laptop deals around.

The 13-inch MacBook Air M4 features the same elegant design as its predecessors, along with excellent M4-driven performance and epic battery life. This starting configuration comes with 16GB of RAM and a 512GB SSD. Right now you can get $250 off, which is a great discount.

The Ring Video Doorbell (2nd Gen) now comes in a slimmer shell, and new colorways — this one has a speckled gray finish. You get Retinal 2K video, 6x zoom and two-way talk. This deal gets you two video doorbells.

Blink's outdoor camera offering, the Outdoor 4, comes with 1080p HD real-time footage, infrared night vision, two-way audio and a wider field of view, so you can see all the nooks and crannies outside your home. The camera also features dual-zone detection and comes with a Blink Sync Module 2, so you can store your footage locally.

Nintendo's Black Friday deal is live! The whole world may be swooning over GTA 6 but this bundle gets you a Nintendo Switch 2 console, a copy of Mario Kart World, and a 3-month Nintendo Switch online membership for $499. That saves you a total of $87 if you'd bought everything separately. This is the same price that was offered at launch, before the Switch 2 got a price hike, so be aware of that going in — but considering how expensive rival consoles are these days, the Switch 2 still offers the best value for money.

Another collection that's a must have for series fans! This collection brings a pair of excellent stealth action games to the Switch 2 for the first time. You'll also be able to enjoy improved graphics, performance and bonus content.

If you want to stay up to date with 2K's NBA action, you can get the 2027 version of the game on sale right now. This edition of the game brings the option to play at 60fps in performance mode, which is a nice upgrade. Playing on Switch 2, the graphics don't look as good as on the other consoles, but you're sacrificing fidelity for the option to play on the go.

Control Resonant surpasses its excellent predecessor thanks to its larger scope, both narratively and gameplay-wise. The melee-based combat is appropriately brutal and engaging, while the various skill trees offer a deep level of customization.

Sony’s standard PS5 pad remains one of the best controllers around thanks to its responsive haptic feedback and adaptive triggers. Standard colorways, including white, midnight black, cosmic red, and galactic purple, are down to $54 here, beating PlayStation Direct’s sale price.

The Gel-Kayano is Asics' flagship stability running shoe, offering extra support for overpronators on the run. My colleague (and a sub-2:30 marathon runner) Nick tested the newer Asics Gel-Kayano 33, and while it has some notable updates, he still tells me the Gel-Kayano 32 is the better buy thanks to this deal.

Hands down my favorite hair styling tool I’ve tested in 2026, the Steamlift Pro has dropped from $129 to $99. If you want a more affordable option than Dyson or Shark without sacrificing results, grab it while it’s under $100 for bouncy, snag-free '90s volume using steam rather than dry heat.

Un ottimo Tomori, Amorim: "Ho cambiato idea rispetto a inizio stagione, sono grato"

📅 Nov 26, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Dalla partita di Atene, vinta dal Milan in rimonta contro l'Olympiacos ad Atene per 2-4, oltre alla reazione di orgoglio, ai tre punti e alle cose da migliorare evidenziate da Amorim a fine gara, la formazione rossonera si porta a casa anche il convincente ingresso di Fikayo Tomori da difensore centrale. L'inglese ha sostituito De Winter dopo il 2-0 con grande personalità e il giusto agonismo. In conferenza stampa Ruben Amorim ha elogiato proprio Fikayo Tomori che, tra l'altro, rientrava da un infortunio.

"Penso che possiamo considerare tutti titolari. Oggi ha la velocità, ed oggi è importante. Poi ha l'esperienza. Quando entra in campo fa il suo lavoro. Non è importante l'età che ha, può migliorare tanto, si può adattare centrale. Ho cambiato idea rispetto ad inizio stagione, e sono grato di questo. Situazioni come genere cambiano la nostra stagione, e sono contento. Ha recuperato da un infortunio e oggi era pronto, mentalmente, e dimostra la sua personalità. Lui ha molta esperienza, ha esperienza, e sono grato dello staff medico per questo".

Wouter Vrancken has stressed Hearts’ objective remains the same despite conceding a last-minute goal that led to an agonising defeat against AS Monaco at Tynecastle.

The Tynecastle manager was not giving up on anything after the 3-2 loss, with United States World Cup star Folarin Balogun scoring the winning goal in the final seconds of added time.

Hearts had taken the lead after a sensational strike from Jordi Altena on 15 minutes. A penalty from Balogun levelled things before the visitors took the lead with a goal from Edam Diop five minutes before half time. Sabah Kerjota scored the goal of the night on the stroke of half-time after curling in with his left foot to leave everything to play for in the second half.

“I think the point doesn't make a difference,” said Vrancken. “There's also something that really was pleasing for me is that when it was 2-2, we still wanted to go (for the win).

"You saw also when it was a throw-in, we wanted to do it fast, we wanted to go for the win. Against a side like this, in the situation we're in, I am so really proud of this also.

"Three points would make a difference," he added. "Zero or one point doesn't make a difference towards the next games, so you have to win the next games. One point or no points doesn't change anything in the next games.”

The Belgian stressed his pride in his players and reiterated that Hearts were missing nine injured players as well as Leart Kabashi and Eduardo Ageu, who were not named in the European squad. He did, however, lament the lack of concentration that saw them concede so late in the game after 93-and-a-half minutes of lung-busting effort. He was also unhappy that Hearts were not cute enough to stop Monaco in their tracks as they broke free for the winning goal. Substitute Finlay Pollock had the chance to clip Mamadou Coulibaly’s heels before the midfielder played in Balogun. Ruthlessness might be something Hearts are lacking at this level. A reporter pointed out that it was a cruel way to lose a match.

“It did feel like this,” said Vrancken. “But at the same time, we have to learn in that situation because I think until then we were really solid about giving chances away. And I expect more from guys who come in from the side (substitutes).

“We can win it with a fresh player and in the middle we can win it with a fresh player. Or you make a foul somewhere to keep the result - I expect this. This is like battling for the team, as I call it.

“We have to do better there,” he added. “But the biggest thing, of course, is to be really proud of what performance we put on the park today, because it's against a really good side. Knowing that we have still nine injuries - I will name it - and we have a lot of players not on the European list today and still do this against that team. I'm really proud of what we did.”

He hailed the quality of his side’s goals. “You see also the confidence those guys have. This is what we wanted after the weekend, of course - that you take some confidence from the dynamics of what we did there. I think the conviction around the box was there, in both boxes actually. It's an important thing to take with us towards the next games coming, especially in this run of games.”

Hearts host Celtic, who beat them 7-1 last month, at Tynecastle on Sunday. Vrancken is firmly in the belief that his side have their mojo back following this and the 5-2 defeat to Falkirk earlier this month. Hearts have since beaten Dundee 8-0 and been edged out by Monaco in a five-goal thriller. “We have played two good games and two good performances against good sides, especially today,” he said. “And now you have the confidence. But we are still playing against a good side on Sunday with only two days' rest, so we have to manage fatigue and make sure that we are as fresh as possible again to make up for something a few weeks ago, especially because it's an at-home game.”

Monaco manager Filipe Luis, meanwhile, denied that relief was the primary emotion after leaving it so late to collect three points. “It is not relief, we compete to win,” he said. “We had an amazing opportunity to win tonight but we had a tough opponent.

“They scored two unbelievable goals,” he added. “You almost need to applaud them. When a team scores two goals like this it is almost nobody’s fault. They are two fantastic goals. Honestly, it’s very beautiful.”

He spoke admiringly of the atmosphere. “I played against Celtic (with Atletico Madrid) in 2011 I think in the Europa League,” he said. “We are lucky to have the opportunity to play these types of games in different countries. It is so intense. I am happy to have had this opportunity to be here tonight – and happy with the result.”

Should You Buy Tesla Stock Before December?

📅 Nov 26, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Merger talks might jolt Tesla stock by year-end, or they might now.

By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:15PM EST

Tesla (TSLA -1.18%) has had a challenging year. Despite its core electric vehicle (EV) business often performing better than expected, partly due to soaring oil prices, the company's shares have significantly lagged broader equities. However, the year isn't over, and there is a chance Tesla could finish 2026 with a bang, given ongoing developments. With that said, should investors consider buying the stock before December?

Tesla's CEO, Elon Musk, now leads two publicly traded corporations, the other being Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%), which went public in June. Rumors of a potential merger between Tesla and SpaceX have been circulating since before SpaceX was public, but a comment Musk made during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call added fuel to the fire.

Musk said that SpaceX and Tesla have formed independent special committees to discuss a potential merger between the two corporations. And more recently, five board directors from both companies have reportedly been discussing a potential all-stock merger that would make the combined entity worth about $3.5 trillion, with a deal possible by year-end. Importantly, this hasn't been confirmed by either company. But it's still worth figuring out the potential benefits and risks of this proposed acquisition.

Suppose SpaceX acquires Tesla at a 20% premium in an all-stock deal: SpaceX would have to issue a substantial number of new shares, thereby significantly diluting existing shareholders. Tesla's stock might rise, at least initially, while SpaceX's could decline unless investors believe the merger will generate enough synergies to justify the acquisition premium.

There are indeed some reasons to think that the combined entity could create more value than either would on its own. For instance, both Tesla and SpaceX are investing massive sums in artificial intelligence (AI). As a single entity, they could eliminate redundant investments and lower costs, while leveraging their larger size to negotiate better deals with suppliers.

Also, some of Tesla's work, including its energy infrastructure and the Optimus humanoid robot, could be of immense value to SpaceX. So, that could be good news for the business' long-term prospects, although whether the proposed combined entity will, on balance, create more value is by no means guaranteed. However, one major source of uncertainty will likely come from regulators. The deal will probably attract significant attention from lawmakers, at least some of whom may try to stop it.

Whether they succeed or not, it's hard to predict the impact on Tesla and SpaceX. And even as a combined entity, the company will be significantly exposed to regulatory risk across businesses such as space launch, satellite-based connectivity, EVs, and robotaxis.

Putting aside the acquisition talks, Tesla's own business has somewhat attractive prospects. The company's work in the robotaxi industry looks promising. Tesla launched the Cybercab, a self-driving vehicle with no steering wheel, no pedals, and no mirrors, earlier this year. Provided it can scale its Cybercab fleet and capture a decent share of the market over the next five to 10 years, the robotaxi business could meaningfully contribute to the company's revenue and profits.

And Tesla does have an advantage over other robotaxi leaders. The company has a growing number of subscriptions to its Full Self-Driving software, which it offers to EV owners for $99 per month. A growing FSD ecosystem grants the company access to more data to train and improve its software. And as Tesla has pointed out, the FSD software is becoming one of the reasons people buy Teslas. That's great news for the company's future.

But one of Tesla's problems is valuation. At 157.3x forward earnings, the market has already priced in significant success from the company's robotaxi ambition. So, I'd be skeptical about buying Tesla's shares at current levels. I'd prefer a much lower price. The potential merger with SpaceX changes very little, in my view, and actually adds significantly more uncertainty to the mix.

The combined entity (if a merger does happen) will certainly be worth serious consideration, but investors with an average tolerance for risk and volatility shouldn't buy Tesla stock right now, whether or not they expect the company to merge with SpaceX.

Steel costs and rate pressure are delaying the storage builds that feed Janus's volumes, and that tension is the part long-term holders must weigh.

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:07PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Janus International Group ›

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings conference call, held on Nov. 10, 2026, Janus International Group (JBI +1.34%) lowered its full-year revenue guidance to between $855 million and $865 million. A sharp slowdown in self-storage development tests whether the manufacturer can defend its margins through cost cuts and technology sales when construction activity turns sluggish. Three takeaways from management's comments show how the business is adapting.

Higher input costs and financing rates squeeze developers' margins, forcing customers to delay construction of new facilities. That pause directly cuts into delivery volumes for self-storage building components.

When top-line volume drops, structural cost reductions help protect profitability. Management cut expenses across operations and manufacturing to align its cost footprint with lower market demand.

Management is expanding its Noke Smart Entry platform, a technology-enabled access control system for self-storage facilities, to build recurring digital revenue. Adding tech content to existing sites creates recurring revenue opportunities beyond physical steel doors.

Demand remains under pressure across North American self-storage channels, and market conditions show no immediate signs of recovery. Janus relies on its broad customer distribution and technology adoption to defend market share while maintaining pricing discipline.

Disciplined capital allocation and cash generation remain central priorities while new project starts lag.

Blizzard's latest patch prevents Alterac Valley from being a glorified reputation farm.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Despite being set in the past, WoW: Forever is an attempt to capture the spirit of the old game by injecting it with new quirks that challenge new and returning players alike to approach it differently than any other version of the MMO. This is why familiar old dungeons can drop new loot, like an armor set that turns you into a snake.

Blizzard has said that its goal is to "unsolve" the game as best it can so players don't settle into the same routines they're used to. This is especially true for min-maxed strategies that threaten to suck the fun out of enjoying the game, or "the journey", as Blizzard likes to call it.

It's a lofty goal that can't be achieved without persistently fiddling with the knobs that encourage players to do one thing over another—which is the very thing that differentiates WoW: Forever from WoW Classic.

This week, Blizzard stepped in to fix a problem that was brewing in its 40-player MOBA-esque PvP mode Alterac Valley. Players were avoiding PvP altogether, turning it into a glorified reputation farm.

"We’ve seen that players in Alterac Valley were frequently completing the battleground without capturing the objectives, so we’ve made some adjustments to incentivize a focus on the objectives rather than rushing to kill the enemy faction’s general," community manager Kaivax wrote.

The patch basically broke a popular 'zerg' strategy where one side rushed to end the match as fast as possible by beefing up the NPC defenders that stood in their way. Blizzard shifted some of the reputation and honor you'd normally get from killing the generals to the other objectives so players are encouraged to engage with the whole mode.

But, as I've seen with changes like this in the past few weeks, many players are upset that they can't just spam it for the rewards, and that others have already reaped the benefits of the old strategy. There are people in Reddit threads doing the math to highlight how much efficiency has been lost (it doesn't seem like much) and questioning the point of doing Alterac Valley at all.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

While I sympathize with not wanting to do something that feels like a chore, it's a far worse problem to have an entire part of the game flattened into an AFK farm. Alterac Valley is supposed to feel like a large-scale war where you look at a big map and choose what objectives are worth fighting over as you try to weaken the enemy forces. The loot you get from maxing out your reputation with the associated factions is meant to be a reward for putting in the effort to learn what it takes to win.

The whole pitch for WoW: Forever is that it's not going to ditch everything with a new expansion every few years. Numbers can be tweaked down the line if the reputation grind is too much of a slog, but the mode should be fun to play so it's not treated like a box to check off in your character's journey. An inert PvP mode ruins the spirit of the MMO far more than a slightly longer reputation grind does.

I think this is a good example of a healthy change that shows Blizzard is committed to protecting core parts of the experience from becoming a treadmill that nobody enjoys. WoW: Forever's strengths are the ways it encourages you to participate in systems that aren't there to fill progression bars. As Harvey said in his WoW: Forever review, "Forever is proof that old-school MMO design deserves a second chance," and that requires taking a stance on what the game is and isn't meant to be.

Doncaster Rovers 2 Huddersfield Town 3: 10-man Terriers emphatically end their barren league streak at bogey venue

📅 Nov 26, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Certainly for the victor, if there happens to be one.

Do the business, put your feet up - well, sort of - with three points in the bag ahead of a long weekend and watch the rest of your divisional rivals sweat it out.

That was the hope for both Doncaster Rovers and Huddersfield Town in their differing third-tier missions.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The incentive for Rovers was moving out of the drop zone up to 18th, while Town’s ambition revolved around securing the win that would draw them level with leaders Stockport County at the right end of the table.

Huddersfield were the ones smiling as they finally made hay at league level at what had previously been a bogey ground.

The first ever visitors here back on New Year’s Day 2007 - the 20th anniversary is in a month’s time - Town had not so much as scored in any of their previous four visits at league level.

They emphatically put paid to that on a night when they played with a man light for around an hour. You didn’t really guess.

For the first 34 minutes, this game simply wasn’t a contest. There were 19 places between these two rivals ahead of kick-off and it showed as Town cruised into a 2-0 lead, courtesy of Cameron Humphreys’ first goal of the campaign and a 15th strike of a goal-laden season for Joe Taylor before Bali Mumba’s Donny demons resurfaced.

In the league fixture here in February, a panicking handball saw him concede a penalty in the game-breaking moment.

In the present, he was the guilty party again - towards the same goal. He hauled down Jamie Sterry, who got on the wrong side of him following Robbie Gotts’ spotter’s badge of a pass.

Booked earlier for a sliding challenge he couldn’t complain about, Mumba was dismissed for a second yellow card—his second dismissal of the season.

Isaac Hutchinson sent the underemployed Matt Young the wrong way to make it 2-1 and out of nowhere, we had a game on.

But Town, not Rovers, grabbed the all-important fourth goal.

Unconvincing at the back, the hosts erred for a third time and Ilias Bronkhurst fired in a soothing third.

Even without an extra player, it was Town who had the wit going forward as Rovers lacked penetration and quality. Given their defensive charity, it wasn’t a good mix and it's easy to see why they are where they are in the standings.

A stoppage-time goal from home captain Owen Bailey revived Rovers, but it was not enough. Nowhere near.

Rovers, without the ineligible Alfie May under the terms of his loan, handed a first start to loanee James Collins, now finally over his long-term knee injury.

It was a psychologically important night for the veteran striker, who was injured almost exactly a year to the day on December 2, 2025 - ironically against Town. It was his last start.

Collins, who turns 36 on Tuesday, was afforded an early birthday present in the process. Sterry also returned to the Rovers’ starting line-up following illness. Brandon Hanlan dropped to the bench, with Tom Nixon absent.

Joe Low and Fletcher - lined up from the off for Town, coming in for Ibane Bowat and Bojan Radulovic.

Ahead of the game, Martin Drury had spoken about Rovers’ set-piece threat, with Low’s promotion seemingly something to do with that.

A gulf in class saw Town stroll most of the first-half, aided by the meek defensive tendencies which Rovers had avoided five days earlier at Bradford City. It eventually changed.

The promotion of Ashley Fletcher, who had delivered a fine cameo in the Trophy game here in early autumn - looked the shrewdest of moves from Drury.

He teed up Humphreys for an easy low finish for Town’s opener on five minutes after Mumba’s cross caused initial consternation as Rovers prevaricated at the back terribly.

Town mixed play up impressively and afforded themselves plenty of control and possession.

Last-ditch defending from ex-Terriers man Matty Pearson blocked Bronkhorst’s goalbound effort. A similarly alert block from Jack Senior repeated the trick to deny Low.

Town’s second was not long in coming on 21 minutes with Rovers again spooked by Fletcher, who showed adept chest control and neat footballing skills to set up Taylor, who fired home a clinical low volley as Rovers again stood and watched.

A brief half-chant of 'We turn up, why don't you' arrived from disgruntled Rovers patrons in the Black Bank.

Mumba’s indiscretion changed the complexion of the night and Thomas spurned a chance to level before the break, planting a free header over.

Ahead of the resumption, Grant McCann threw on another attack-minded player in Hakeeb Adelakun. His side saw a lot of the ball in the opening part of the second period, but couldn’t conjure a big chance against 10-man Town.

It was the visitors, who still possessed the killer instinct.

Sanches Fernandes rattled the crossbar and from the resultant corner, Rovers’ defensive deficiencies again re-surfaced.

The ball found Bronkhorst and after his initial effort was blocked, he rammed home a low drive in front of the ecstatic 1,905 Terriers supporters.

Bailey ensured there was a nervy finale for the visitors, firing home from Adelakun's low cross. But it was Town's night, deservedly.

Doncaster Rovers: Simkin; Sterry, Grehan (Ayinde 70), Pearson, Senior, Thomas (Husband 84); Gotts, Bailey, Broadbent (Adelakun HT), Hutchinson (O’Reilly 65); J Collins (Hanlan 65). Substitutes unused: Clarke, Bryne. Huddersfield Town: Young; Balker, Low, Roughan; Bronkhorst, A Collins (Ledson 69), Humphreys, Mumba, Sanches Fernandes (Bowat 84), Taylor (Radulovic 84); Fletcher (Harness 55). Substitutes unused: Alnwick, Gooch, Ashia.

Attendance: 8,376 (1,905 Huddersfield Town supporters).
